title: Why people have different skin colors

paragraphs: Human skin tones vary globally due to our long evolutionary relationship with ultraviolet (UV) radiation. Near the equator, high UV levels led to dark pigmentation with abundant melanin, which protects DNA from solar damage.

However, as human ancestors migrated to regions with significantly lower UV levels, high melanin became a health disadvantage. Some UV wavelengths are essential for synthesizing vitamin D, a key nutrient required for strong bones and a healthy immune system. To ensure survival in low-UV environments, human skin adapted by becoming lighter. Additionally, people with moderate skin tones developed the ability to tan by producing melanin during sunnier summer months and losing it in winter.

Today, because people migrate rapidly across different regions, many must consciously manage their relationship with the sun through lifestyle choices, including using skin protection or taking vitamin D supplements.

paragraphs: Humans have different skin colors because people from the past lived under different levels of sunlight. Near the equator, where light from the sun is very strong, dark skin protected people’s bodies.

When humans moved to places with less sun, dark skin made it hard to make enough vitamin D. We need vitamin D to build strong bones and stay healthy. Over time, skin color changed and became lighter so people could make vitamin D even with less sunlight. Some people can also tan, which means their skin gets darker in summer and lighter in winter.
Today, people travel and live all around the world. Because of this, some people need to protect their skin from the sun, while others need to take extra vitamin D pills to stay healthy.

paragraphs: People have different skin colors because of the sun. In very sunny places, dark skin protects people from strong light. But when people move to places with less sun, dark skin is a problem.

The body needs light from the sun to make vitamin D. Vitamin D gives us strong bones and good health. So, human skin becomes lighter in places with less sun. Some people’s skin can also get darker in summer and lighter in winter.
Today, people travel and live everywhere. Sometimes we need to use sun cream to protect our skin. Sometimes we need to take extra vitamins to be healthy.
